artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space (or a Hilbert space) and let $M\subset X$ be a compact subset equipped with a Borel probability measure $\mu$ supported on $M$. For $\varepsilon>0$ and $\delta\in(0,1)$, consider the following entropy-type quantities.

(i) The $\varepsilon$-entropy of the set $M$:
$$H_\varepsilon(M)=\log_2 N_\varepsilon(M),$$
where $N_\varepsilon(M)$ is the minimal number of closed balls of radius $\varepsilon$ needed to cover $M$.

(ii) The measure $\varepsilon$-entropy: choose a minimal $\varepsilon$-cover of $M$ by balls and let $\{C_j\}$ be the associated partition of $M$ into measurable pieces of diameter $\le 2\varepsilon$; set
$$H_\varepsilon(\mu)=-\sum_j \mu(C_j)\log_2\mu(C_j).$$

(iii) The $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-entropy $H_{\varepsilon,\delta}(\mu)$: the logarithm (base $2$) of the minimal number of $\varepsilon$-balls needed to cover a subset of $M$ of $\mu$-measure at least $1-\delta$.

(iv) The variants $\widetilde H_\varepsilon$ and $\widetilde H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$ in which coverings are replaced by packings (maximal collections of pairwise disjoint balls of radius $\varepsilon$ centered in $M$, with the analogous measure-restricted version for $\widetilde H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$).

Problem. Investigate the properties of, and establish the precise relations between, the four entropy functions $H_\varepsilon$, $H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$, $\widetilde H_\varepsilon$, $\widetilde H_{\varepsilon,\delta}$ on compact sets and probability measures in metric or Hilbert spaces. In particular, study their asymptotic behavior as $\varepsilon\to 0$, their invariance (or lack thereof) under isometries, rotations, and smooth deformations of the underlying set $M$, and determine to what extent the leading-order asymptotic
$$H_\varepsilon(\mu)\sim d\log_2(1/\varepsilon)\cdot \mu(X)$$
(observed when $M=Q^d\subset\mathbb R^d$ is the unit cube with $\mu$ the Lebesgue measure) persists when $Q^d$ is embedded and rotated inside a larger space $X^n$, $n>d$, or otherwise deformed.
